subject: Migration PoC: architecture review / technical deep-dive scheduling
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@quantahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Lee <sam.lee@quantahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Migration PoC - request for architecture deep-dive

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team and I were impressed with Redwood's latency/cost story. We're interested in a short Proof-of-Concept to validate migration from our current provider (VendorX) and to evaluate running some components ourselves.

Before we kick off the PoC, our infra and security leads want a 60–90 minute architecture deep-dive to cover:
- high-level serving topology (split between managed vs private)
- data flows and network egress implications
- auth/KMS integration and model artifacts lifecycle
- migration paths for model weights and KV cache priming

Suggested time windows (PST):
- Thu 2026-02-12 10:00–11:30
- Fri 2026-02-13 14:00–15:30

If those don't work, we can propose alternatives. Goal is to have our infra + security + lead engineer present.

A couple quick context points to help prep:
- We're on AWS (us-west-2), using VendorX managed endpoints today for inference of a fine-tuned 13B model (ML-13B).
- Baseline: ~150–250 RPS at 512 tokens, peak bursts to 600 RPS. Target p95 latency for single-token steps ~60–80ms; end-to-end generation latency target ~600–900ms for typical prompts.
- We're considering a hybrid: control plane managed, but dedicated capacity in our VPC for sensitive workloads.

Can you confirm availability and whether an engineer from Redwood (someone who can speak kernel/quant/etc) can join?

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Director of Platform Eng
QuantaHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@quantahealth.com>
Cc: Sam Lee <sam.lee@quantahealth.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Migration PoC - request for architecture deep-dive

Alex — thanks for the context and the clear asks. Happy to run the architecture review and bring the right folks. I've looped in our senior solutions engineer, Dev Patel, who will drive the technical portion. Also adding Rishi from our platform team for networking/KMS notes.

Of your proposed windows, Thu 02/12 10:00–11:30 PST works for us — we can block 90 minutes. If that becomes a conflict I’ll propose alternates.

Prep: we have a short pre-read we can send (architecture checklist + example hybrid topology) and it would help if you can share:
- whether model artifacts are stored in S3 or are still with VendorX
- expected durable KV cache size or whether cache can be relearned during PoC
- any egress constraints or IP allowlist needs for vendor-managed control plane

I’ll schedule a calendar invite for Thu 10:00 PST and include a short agenda.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@quantahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Migration PoC - request for architecture deep-dive

Thanks, Marissa. Alex — quick intro, I’ll be the SE on the call. A couple technical clarifying Qs to make the session efficient:

1) Model artifacts: do you have a dump of the model weights in S3 (recommended) or are they currently hosted only with VendorX? If the latter, do you have contractual ability to export?

2) KV cache: approximate size (number of prefixes / total tokens cached) and whether it is acceptable to re-prime during the PoC (we can do fast priming strategies).

3) Authentication/KMS: do you use a customer-managed KMS (CMK) in your AWS account for keys today, or would you rely on Redwood-managed KMS for the PoC?

4) Network topology: are there strict egress IP allowlists / static IP requirements? If so we’ll present our private deployment VPC peering approach.

From our side, I can present: serving runtime topology (multi-tenant vs dedicated), kernel/quant tradeoffs for 13B at 512 tokens, warm/cold KV strategies, and example throughput-cost estimates.

If Thu 02/12 10:00 PST remains good I’ll send a calendar invite that includes a 6-slide pre-read and a short architecture checklist. If you'd prefer Fri 02/13 afternoon let me know — we can be flexible.

—Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@quantahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Lee <sam.lee@quantahealth.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Migration PoC - request for architecture deep-dive

Hi Marissa / Dev — quick update: our infra lead just flagged a conflict on Thu morning for execs who need to be there. Can we shift to Fri 02/13 14:00–15:30 PST instead? That window is the only time the security and infra folks are both available.

Answers to your questions:
- Model artifacts: VendorX currently hosts the weights; we have a 30-day export clause in the contract and can get a copy into our S3 prior to the PoC kickoff (working that now).
- KV cache: currently ~1.2M tokens of useful prefix data; we can provide a sample dump if helpful. Re-priming acceptable but we'd rather avoid rebuilding from scratch.
- KMS: we use a customer-managed CMK in our account. For the PoC we prefer to keep keys in our account.
- Network: we have strict egress rules; we need to allowlist any vendor-managed control-plane IPs.

If Fri 02/13 14:00 PST works for you all, confirm and we’ll accept the invite.

Thanks,
Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
